change.describe: branch `pr-37634` of keycloak-37634 against c22f76867f595f0f7c327376a66a08dca01949e8 (merge-base c22f768)
change.title: pr-37634
change.description:
Encoding context to access token IDs closes #37118
Shorter encoding of access token
change.author: mposolda

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher checks the wrong characters and with inverted logic
findings.body: The encoded id is `<st:2><tt:2><gt:2>:<uuid>`, so the grant shortcut is `items[0].substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. The condition is also inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects a match. For `onrtac` the slice (3,5) is `ta`, so the matcher passes for any shortcut that does not happen to appear at that offset. It never verifies the grant, and it could reject a correct id by coincidence. It is used in expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken, so none of them test the grant encoding. Fix: `if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. The `describeTo` text should also say what was expected, not just 'Not a Token ID'.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` is a copy/paste slip: it should check `rawTokenId`. A null rawTokenId is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` then produces an id like `onrtac:null`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of a NullPointerException, not the intended IllegalArgumentException
findings.body: The test never calls `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` in the factory is null. For the unknown shortcut `ac`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls into its refresh branch and calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:125), which throws an NPE. The `catch (RuntimeException)` swallows it, so the test passes without exercising the 'Unknown value ... for grant type' path. Catch `IllegalArgumentException` and provide a mocked or stubbed `KeycloakSessionFactory` that returns an empty stream. Other gaps: there is no test for `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`, a context part that is not 6 chars long, or unknown session-type or token-type shortcuts. The `assertEquals` calls also have expected and actual swapped (e.g. lines 56-59), which gives misleading failure messages.

findings.title: Shortcut contract says '3-letters' but the encoder only works with exactly 2 characters, and nothing validates it
findings.body: The javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut'. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the context part to be exactly 6 chars (2+2+2) and slices the grant shortcut as `substring(4, 6)` (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-81). `encodeTokenId` does no length check, and `postInit` (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:70-85) only checks duplicates. A custom grant factory that follows the javadoc and returns a 3-letter shortcut, or null, gets access tokens issued whose ids cannot be decoded later (IllegalArgumentException 'Expected length of 6'). A null shortcut puts null into the ConcurrentHashMap and throws an NPE during startup. Fix: document 'exactly 2 characters', and validate non-null and length 2 in `postInit` and in the lazy refresh in `getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut`. This is also a new abstract method on a public SPI interface, so out-of-tree OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations break at load time (AbstractMethodError). The only implementations in this repo are the ones updated here.

findings.title: Unused import
findings.body: `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` is imported but never used in this file. The attribute is set with `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE`.

findings.title: GRANT_TYPE attribute is set twice for the password grant
findings.body: `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` is set here and again in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109) with the same value. One of the two is redundant. Setting it in a single place keeps the mechanism easy to follow, because the attribute is currently set in four different styles: createTokenResponse, TokenManager.refreshAccessToken, StandardTokenExchangeProvider and PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.

contracts.action: Access token `jti` is now generated as `<session><token><grant>:<uuid>` via the new TokenContextEncoderProvider instead of a plain UUID
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` in initToken; all createClientAccessToken callers (TokenManager:613, KeycloakIdentity:148, PolicyEvaluationService:289, AccessTokenResponseBuilder.generateAccessToken:1205)
contracts.before_after: Before: random UUID. After: the encoder reads GRANT_TYPE from the ClientSessionContext. Paths that do not set it (implicit/hybrid, policy evaluation, KeycloakIdentity) get shortcut 'na', which is registered in the maps at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory:78-79. The encoder uses `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`, which needs a non-null `session.getContext().getClient()`. DefaultClientSessionContext sets the client at line 94, and the mappers already called this method on the same paths.
contracts.visible_effect: `jti` and event `token_id` detail change format. AssertEvents is updated for this, but its matcher is buggy (see finding).
contracts.failure_mode: An unknown grant id or an unregistered shortcut makes encodeTokenId throw IllegalStateException during token creation, which gives a 500. A custom grant with a shortcut that is not 2 chars issues ids that cannot be decoded (reported).

contracts.action: OAuth2GrantType.Context now captures grant_type from the form params in its constructor; the copy constructor is removed
contracts.equivalent_path: TokenEndpoint builds the Context at TokenEndpoint.java:149 after checkGrantType() has resolved the grant by the same form param
contracts.before_after: The grant is looked up by the same `grant_type` value, so context.getGrantType() equals the factory id. `setFormParams` does not update the cached grantType, but no caller in the repo uses it. A grep found no remaining users of `Context(Context)` or subclasses of Context.
contracts.visible_effect: None directly; it feeds the GRANT_TYPE attribute.
contracts.failure_mode: If a later caller replaces form params through setFormParams, grantType stays stale.

contracts.action: Lazy refresh of grant shortcut maps when an unknown grant or shortcut is seen
contracts.before_after: The postInit path runs the duplicate-shortcut check. The lazy path does not, so a late-deployed grant with a duplicate shortcut silently overwrites the map entry.
contracts.visible_effect: A token id could decode to the wrong grant.
contracts.failure_mode: Edge case, only for dynamically deployed factories.

summary:
The change is mostly sound. The main defects are in the tests and in small validation gaps.

- **Test matcher is wrong.** `isAccessTokenId` in AssertEvents slices the wrong characters and has inverted logic, so the four events that use it don't verify the grant shortcut.
- **Wrong null check.** `AccessTokenContext` checks `grantType` twice and never checks `rawTokenId`.
- **Test passes for the wrong reason.** `testIncorrectGrantType` throws an NPE (the session factory is never initialised) and catches it as a `RuntimeException`, so the intended unknown-grant path is never exercised.
- **Shortcut contract.** The `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` javadoc says '3-letters', but the encoder only decodes exactly 2 characters, and nothing validates this.
- **Minor.** There is an unused import and a redundant double-set of the grant attribute.
